sourceFacts: Children with proximal pelvic-girdle weakness may use their arms to assist rising.
The Gowers manoeuvre includes pushing on the thighs to raise the trunk.
prompt:
Create a polished original medical teaching illustration in landscape 3:2 format. Use the attached MD3 original solely as a style reference: warm watercolour/gouache on an ivory paper background, delicate ink contours, calm navy labels, muted ochre/peach/teal colours, generous whitespace and clear flat anatomical shapes. Anatomical clarity before decoration. Never photorealistic skin, glossy blood, wet flesh, fat lobules, scary faces, chunky 3D tissue blocks, or a fake scan. Only exact requested labels, clean legible short text. Footer 'Educational schematic'. No watermark, logos or attribution in the pixels. Compose an entirely new subject from the clinical specification, not the scalp content in the reference.

A four-step left-to-right movement sequence of the SAME clothed young child in teal t-shirt and ochre shorts. Profile/three-quarter views keep body mechanics clear. Step1 child on hands and knees. Step2 feet planted with hips high, both hands on floor in bear stance. Step3 trunk partly raised, knees mostly extended, both hands pressing onto own thighs just above knees. Step4 child nearly standing, hands higher on own thighs near hips to push torso upright. No hands pressing shins in final step, no extra limbs, no furniture support. Numbered small labels '1', '2', '3', '4'. Gentle arrows between steps. Title 'Gowers manoeuvre'. Bottom 'The hands help lift the trunk when hip-girdle muscles are weak'. No claim unique to Duchenne.
